correctness.rationale: Braun's centered radial semimartingale and Barenblatt coefficient have the exact self-similar scaling used in the package. Under logarithmic time and \(Y_s=e^{-s/\beta}r_{e^s}\), direct Itô calculation makes the coefficient time-homogeneous. For \(J=(\kappa/C)Y^q\), the diffusion coefficient simplifies to \(2KJ(1-J)\) and the drift to \(K\{\alpha-(\alpha+\eta)J\}\); independent symbolic reduction confirms \(K=pM/((p-1)^2\beta)\) and \(q/(\beta K)=\gamma\). Braun's Proposition 3.20 transforms exactly to the Beta \((\alpha,\eta)\) marginal. Standard one-dimensional uniqueness for the square-root Jacobi coefficient identifies the scalar path law, and the centered first Jacobi eigenfunction gives the exact exponential covariance in log time, hence \((s/t)^\Lambda\) in physical time.
residual_risks: The scalar path-law identification does not establish any Markov or uniqueness property for the full nonlinear vector process.
